links.outcome: Diagnostic recall of single LLMs and multi-agent systems compared with each other and physicians on same cases
links.effect: Single GPT-oss-20b scored 4.68 vs Adaptive multi-agent 4.13 (p<0.001); Adaptive system did not outperform median physician score of 4.22 (p=0.432).
links.quote: The Adaptive System, despite utilising dynamic routing, failed to outperform the median score of human physicians (4.22 [SD 3.62]; p = 0.432).

links.outcome: Accuracy, safety, and latency of complex multi-agent systems versus simpler single model
links.effect: Single GPT-oss-20b outperformed multi-agent ensembles; safety score 5.50 vs 4.99 (p<0.001); Top-1 accuracy 51.58% vs 46.89%; latency 30s vs 200s (85% reduction).
links.quote: Furthermore, the inclusion of mid-tier models in the adaptive workflow introduced an "ensemble degradation" effect, significantly lowering the Safety Score compared to the single GPT-oss-20b model (4.99 vs 5.50; p < 0.001) and reducing the rate of Top-1 correct diagnoses from 51.58% to 46.89%.

unlisted_practices: Preferring a single locally hosted open-source LLM over multi-agent ensembles for offline, resource-constrained settings

screen.reason: The study compares different AI model architectures (single open-source LLMs vs. multi-agent ensemble systems) on an offline clinical diagnosis benchmark dataset. Comparing agent architectures and model configurations alone does not test an organizational deployment practice or operational safeguard.
